leftEvidence.title: Boasting only in the cross

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Paul contrasts those who compel circumcision with his own refusal to boast except in the cross, then speaks of new creation, peace, marks, grace, and the world crucified in relation to him.
points.right: Hearers are urged to run while looking to Jesus, who endured the cross, despised shame, sat at God’s right hand, and endured hostility.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.

payload.posture: The cross appears as the exclusive ground of boasting in one passage and as endured shame in another.

rightEvidence.title: Enduring the cross and despising shame

payload.tension: Galatians contrasts circumcision, persecution, world, and new creation; Hebrews places cross and shame inside an appeal to run with endurance.
